prompt_demand: Calculate two actual lengths from supplied image sizes and magnifications, then compare them to conclude which cell is larger.
reason: The task is a calculation followed by a comparison; nothing is completed (no table or diagram to fill in), so 'complete' does not describe it. 'Calculate' is on the syllabus list and matches the guidance (marks for working out both lengths). AO2 and Analyse stay. Flag: changing the command word may change the tariff rules applied to this slot.
uncertainty: medium: keep 'complete' if the workspace uses 'complete' for INTERP slots by convention, or if the tariff rules for 'calculate' would not allow the comparison mark.

prompt_demand: Interpret three supplied endpoint times by working out the unequal intervals and explain why they do not support a constant-speed model.
reason: The learner breaks down supplied results (works out the 15 s and 21 s intervals) and judges whether they fit a model. That is analysis of data rather than applying a rule. AO3 (C3/C4) stays.
uncertainty: medium: keep Apply if the workspace's Bloom convention labels every APP-subtype item Apply whatever its demand.

prompt_demand: Four-part structured question: state the osmosis definition, name isotonic, describe turgor in a dilute solution, and predict and explain plasmolysis in concentrated salt solution.
reason: Parts (a)-(c) are recall and taught description; (d) applies taught osmosis knowledge to predict plasmolysis. No part asks the learner to break down data or relationships, so Analyse overstates the demand and Apply is the highest level reached. AO1+AO2 kept (see uncertainty). Note: 'state' fits only part (a); no single syllabus command word covers all four parts, so I propose no command-word change.
uncertainty: medium: Analyse could be justified only if (d) counted as interpreting a microscope observation. The AO2 share is itself a boundary, because (d) is close to taught plasmolysis (A).

prompt_demand: Describe the taught sequence for finding a specimen with a light microscope (low power, clip slide, focus, centre).
reason: This is a written description of a taught operating technique. It fits C1 (knowledge of how to use apparatus, following a sequence) and also A3 (techniques of operation). The C1 reading is defensible, so keep AO3. Note that the food-test PROC items (3-189 to 3-193) are labelled AO1 for a similar kind of demand.
uncertainty: medium: would change to AO1 if the workspace decides written recall of an apparatus procedure is A3 rather than C1. Either way, keep it consistent with 3-189 to 3-193.

prompt_demand: Explain the taught reason (field of view) for locating a specimen at low power first.
reason: This is a rehearsed explanation of a technique, close to A3. C1 is defensible because it explains a step in how to use the microscope correctly.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator treats taught rationale for apparatus use as A3.

prompt_demand: Judge a learner's conclusion from a comparison where temperature and shaking both changed, and explain why it is not justified.
reason: B5 (reasoned explanation in a new situation) fits. So does C5/C4 (evaluating whether a comparison controls variables), because the flaw is an uncontrolled variable. The objective is not a practical one, so B is reasonable. Evaluate would also be a defensible Bloom label for judging a conclusion.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO3 and Evaluate if the operator treats every uncontrolled-variable critique as method evaluation regardless of the objective.

prompt_demand: Subtract the supplied concentrations to compare two gradients (6 vs 2 units) and state which has faster net diffusion.
reason: The processing is minimal (one subtraction) and the conclusion is the taught gradient rule, which is near the 'a table alone does not make it B' boundary. It still needs the supplied numbers to be turned into a gradient comparison (B3/B4), so B is defensible.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator judges trivial arithmetic on supplied values insufficient for B.

prompt_demand: Explain observed firmness and softness of pumpkin strips after soaking in water and in sugar solution using osmosis and turgor.
reason: The explanation is the taught osmosis and turgor account (A1), but it is applied to practical observations, which is C4. C is defensible given the practical objective.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator requires processing of observations or data, not just an observed outcome, for C4.

prompt_demand: Infer from supplied gain or loss results that the cell-content concentration lies between 0.1 and 0.2 mol/dm3, and justify it.
reason: AO3 (C4 conclusion from data) is right. On Bloom, Analyse (interpreting a results pattern) and Apply (applying the no-net-change principle) are both defensible.
uncertainty: low on AO; medium on Bloom: Analyse would be preferred if the 3-151 Bloom change is accepted, for consistency.

prompt_demand: Explain mineral deficiency in flooded maize by linking low soil oxygen to less respiration and less active transport.
reason: This is a reasoned explanation of a field situation (B5/B7). However, the taught CHAIN answer for 3-169 already states that waterlogged soil lacking oxygen reduces uptake, so the item is close to rehearsed A content.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if learners are taught the flooding example explicitly. It stays B if 3-169 is the only place it appears and the item needs the link to be built.

prompt_demand: Link many mitochondria in villus cells to active uptake of glucose needing respiratory energy.
reason: AO1 is defensible because the link is taught: 3-171's answer states that these cells have many mitochondria because active transport needs energy. This contrasts with the sibling 3-135 (AO2), where the learner must infer which unfamiliar cell does more work.
uncertainty: low-medium: would move to AO2 only if the villus-mitochondria link is not part of taught content.

prompt_demand: Explain why an enzyme acts on substrate P but not Q (similar size, different binding shape) using active-site fit.
reason: Most of the answer is taught specificity (lock and key), which is A. The 'similar size but different shape' twist asks the learner to separate size from shape, a small piece of reasoning that keeps B defensible.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator views fit and specificity applied to labelled substrates as a rehearsed account.

prompt_demand: Explain why a powder removing a protein stain does not show it removes an oily stain equally well, using enzyme specificity.
reason: The content is taught specificity (protease vs lipase), which is A. It is framed as limiting a conclusion drawn from an investigation result (C4/C5), so C is defensible.
uncertainty: medium: would move to AO1 if the operator wants C reserved for items that process method details or data.
